research.recommended_topic: Last-Minute Tax Saving Mistakes Salaried Indians Make Before March 31
research.audience_problem: Salaried young professionals panic-buy sub-optimal ULIPs, high-fee insurance policies, or locked-in funds in March just to satisfy HR tax proof submission deadlines, jeopardizing long-term wealth.
research.why_now: March is the financial year-end crunch period in India when corporate HR departments enforce hard cutoffs for investment proofs, creating acute anxiety over March salary TDS deductions.
research.hook: HR just sent you the final tax-proof deadline email? Stop panic-buying insurance policies you'll regret in 3 months.
supporting_points: New vs. Old Regime reality check: Explaining why the rebate under the New Tax Regime makes frantic 80C investments completely redundant for incomes under ₹7.75 Lakhs.
The Bank RM ULIP Trap: How relationship managers exploit March panic to lock salaried workers into 5-year recurring premium endowment plans with low returns.
Smart, zero-regret moves: Leveraging simple ELSS (3-year lock-in with equity upside) or pure Term Insurance + Section 80D Health Insurance instead of bundled products.
trend_signals: March 31 Financial Year-End (FY 2024-25) cutoff driving peak Google Trends queries for '80C deductions' and 'save tax before March'.
Viral performance of talking-head + greenscreen tax calculator reels breaking down take-home salary comparisons.
Widespread workplace discussions around March TDS deductions hitting take-home payslips.
candidate_topics: New Tax Regime vs Old Tax Regime: Interactive calculator breakdown for salaries from ₹8L to ₹15L
March Appraisal Framework: The 3 metrics young tech professionals need to pitch for a 20%+ hike
How to manage IPL season micro-spending: Food delivery and fantasy league budget traps
research.reasoning: Tax-saving anxiety right before the fiscal year-end triggers universal concern across corporate India. This topic delivers high-utility, panic-resolving value that naturally incentivizes bookmarking/saving and peer-to-peer sharing via DMs, outperforming evergreen advice during the first three weeks of March.

carousel_outline: Slide 1 (Hook): 'Month-end pe balance dekh kar shock lagta hai?' 5 silent money leaks draining your bank account without you noticing.
Slide 2: Leak 1 - The 'Delivery Fee Bachaane Ka Trap'. Adding a ₹250 dessert just to save ₹40 delivery charges on quick commerce apps.
Slide 3: Leak 2 - Zombie Subscriptions. That OTT platform you watched once, cloud storage you forgot, and gym auto-debits quietly deducting ₹499 every month.
Slide 4: Leak 3 - The 'Micro-UPI' Effect. ₹20 chai, ₹50 cold drink, ₹100 snacks. Small QR scans feel invisible until you download the bank statement.
Slide 5: Leak 4 - Sale FOMO. Buying a ₹1,500 shirt on 50% discount when you didn't need it isn't saving ₹1,500—it is spending ₹1,500.
Slide 6: Leak 5 - Late-Night Dopamine Shopping. Scrolling reels at 1 AM and ending up with aesthetic desk organizers you'll never use.
Slide 7 (Action Step): The 48-Hour Rule: Put non-essential cart items on hold for 2 days. 80% of the time, the urge disappears. Your wallet will thank you.
